title: Claude for research

body.text: Researchers can use Claude to speed up several steps:
summarize papers, compare methodologies across several, and help design research questions
— with long context, it reads a whole paper and you can probe any part.

example: "Read this paper and summarize: the research question, the method, the main results, the limitations, and the gap a follow-up could build on"

title: Limits you need to know

body.text: The iron rule of academic work:
the AI can help read, think, and draft, but facts and citations must always be checked against the original
— the AI may misremember a paper's details, and most universities have AI-use policies you must follow.

example: "Use AI to summarize 20 papers to filter which are relevant, then actually read only the 5 that pass — saving time without the risk"

question: Which research steps can Claude help with?

options.text: Summarizing papers, comparing methodology, and designing research questions

question: What must you do with facts and citations from the AI?

options.text: Always check them against the original

question: What's the smart way to use AI to filter papers?

options.text: Have the AI pre-filter, then actually read only the ones that pass
Read nothing and trust the AI completely
Read every one yourself as before

question: Using Claude for research, what limit must you know?

options.text: The AI may be inaccurate; you must verify and cite the real source

question: What is the AI's scope in research?

options.text: Helps search and summarize, but doesn't replace the researcher's verification
